Supports Union and Subtraction via screen picking and re-voxelization [S1].

The evidence explicitly states in Section 2.4 'Real-Time Modification' that the system supports Union and Subtraction operations. It details that a 'screen-pick operation retrieves the depth value from the framebuffer' to determine the world position, and that a 'voxelization shader is executed to re-voxelize the cell' to apply these modifications. This matches every component of the claim.
supported
1.  **STree (Streaming Tree):** A two-level structure [S1].

The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly confirms every fact listed in the claim. It defines the STree as a two-level structure (2D uniform grid containing sparse octrees), specifies the node resolution (64x64x64), details the GPU Voxel Pool allocation (16,384 voxels per page), describes the CPU traversal and LOD error metric (with LOD_factor typically being 8), outlines the GPU voxelization and rendering process (including the 64-bit visibility buffer, Nanite-like reconstruction, and AtomicMin), explains the real-time modification via screen-pick and AABB, and notes the limitation regarding transparent rendering due to atomic operations. Finally, it cites the specific performance metrics (6.0459 ms at 4K on the specified hardware).

It streams appropriate levels of detail into GPU memory using a two-level data structure, storing data linearly to enable efficient real-time editing (Union/Subtraction) [S1].

The claim states that the system streams appropriate levels of detail into GPU memory using a two-level data structure, stores data linearly, and enables efficient real-time editing (Union/Subtraction). The evidence confirms all these points: Section 2.1 describes the 'two-level structure' (2D uniform grid and STree); the Abstract and Section 2.1 mention that it 'stores data linearly'; Section 2.2 explains streaming appropriate LOD to GPU memory; and Section 2.4 explicitly details support for 'Union and Subtraction' operations for real-time modification.

2.  **World Position:** Determine world position $wP$ of $P$ using the inverted camera matrix [S1].

The claim states that the world position $wP$ of $P$ is determined using the inverted camera matrix. Section 2.4 'Real-Time Modification' in Source [S1] explicitly states: 'Subsequently, the world position wP of P is determined using the inverted camera matrix.' This matches the claim exactly.

4.  **Cell Identification:** Identify all STree cells intersecting the AABB [S1].

The claim states that an AABB is computed around the world position wP and all intersecting STree cells are identified for update. Source [S1], Section 2.4 'Real-Time Modification', explicitly states: 'To modify the scene, we must update the STree cells surrounding wP. To achieve this, we compute an Axis-Aligned Bounding Box (AABB) and update all intersecting cells.' This confirms that the evidence supports the claim.

*   **Limitations:** Only supports opaque objects; transparent rendering is unachievable due to atomic operations [S1].

The claim states that the evidence supports the limitations of only supporting opaque objects and that transparent rendering is unachievable due to atomic operations. The provided text explicitly states in the Conclusion section: 'The current design supports only the rendering of opaque objects.
